statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 18% sits in the low band, well below the 25% block threshold, while Stress 41% is moderate after an in-line Bank of Japan hike and ahead of a US quarterly expiration.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is EA_ON and no blocking condition is in force. The narrow danger window spans 13:15-14:30 UTC, covering the US industrial production release, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the first hour of quarterly-expiration trade, which carries the day's highest projected Tail at 24%. Governor Ueda's press conference near 06:30 UTC is a separate multi-stage checkpoint projected at 22-23%. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Bank of Japan delivers an in-line 25bp hike to 1.25% and Nasdaq-100 futures hold a narrow two-sided overnight band on quarterly-expiration day
body:
The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% on a 7-2 vote, the highest level since April 1995 and exactly what money markets had priced. That removes the first stage of the session's main event risk without a surprise. NQ is trading near 29,731, about 12 points or 0.04% below the prior settlement of 29,743, inside a 29,648.00-29,738.00 overnight band as of 03:15 UTC.

The band spans 90 points, or 0.30%, and the structure is two-sided: the low at 29,648.00 was rejected and bought back roughly 80 points before price settled near the upper half of the range. That is the most important current observation, because the Tail score measures a persistent no-retracement price path, and retracement is plainly functioning. Price sitting in the upper part of a band this narrow is not the same as holding a session extreme in a trending market.

The backdrop remains constructive but is latest-session rather than live evidence. The cash Nasdaq-100 closed Thursday at 29,446.98, up 501.92 points or 1.73%, near the top of a 29,305.90-29,494.95 range, completing the recovery from Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision to raise the target range by 25bp to 3.75-4.00% - the first US hike since 2023, on a 12-0 vote. The VIX closed at 15.44, down 12.82%, which is consistent with orderly rather than disorderly repricing. Treasury yields remain the tighter part of the picture, with the 2-year at 4.74% and the 10-year at 5.01% on the latest H.15 observation.

Energy is the live geopolitical thread. WTI is near $101.29 and Brent near $103.97, both down for a third consecutive session as Saudi Arabia signalled it can restore roughly half the capacity of its East-West pipeline within days following the 10-11 September drone strikes, while rerouting exports through the Strait of Hormuz on shuttle vessels. The direction of travel in that story is currently de-escalation, which argues against treating it as a present Tail amplifier even though the underlying situation stays unresolved.

Two checkpoints define the day. Governor Ueda's press conference near 06:30 UTC is the second stage of the BOJ sequence: with roughly 90bp of further tightening priced over twelve months, cautious guidance could produce a sell-the-fact yen unwind that transmits to global equity risk through carry positioning. That is a credible unresolved second-leg mechanism, so the projected path steps into the watch band for those hours, but it is conditional and nothing of the kind has been observed. The second is the 13:30 UTC cash open into a quarterly expiration, alongside industrial production at 13:15 UTC, a Bowman speech at 13:30 UTC and the Leading Index at 14:00 UTC.

The shared cross-asset context file was collected at 01:37 UTC and is both partial and now beyond its freshness window, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so this assessment rests on independently verified sources. Its latest-session breadth reading - all eight tracked megacaps and all seven tracked semiconductors higher - is consistent with the verified 1.73% cash close but is not evidence of live price-path structure and has not been used to raise Tail.

lookbackSummary: All 24 hours to 02:00 UTC are covered by published Claude assessments. Tail opened the window at 19% during Thursday's Asian session, peaked at 26% in the 13:00 UTC hour around the US cash open - the only hour that mapped to an orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES state - and then eased steadily to 17-18% overnight. Stress fell almost continuously from 68% to 40% as the repricing that followed Wednesday's 25bp Federal Reserve hike resolved in an orderly way and implied volatility decayed, with the VIX closing at 15.44, down 12.8%. The dominant mode ran mixed through the early Asian hours, turned trend-up from 07:00 UTC as the cash session rallied 1.73%, and reverted to normal from 22:00 UTC once futures reopened into a narrow two-sided band. Confidence held in a tight 85-88% band throughout, reflecting continuous coverage rather than any single strong signal.
outlookSummary: The projected path holds 18% in the current hour, in which the Bank of Japan hike printed in line, then eases to 19% through the Asian lull before stepping into the watch band for the press-conference sequence: 22% as Governor Ueda begins near 06:30 UTC and a 23% Asian-session peak at 07:00 UTC as the Q&A overlaps the European open. It falls back to 18-19% across the European morning and the US pre-market, then reaches the day's conditional peak of 24% in the 14:00 UTC hour, the first full hour of quarterly-expiration cash trade following a session that closed 1.73% higher near its range top. Two further watch steps follow at 19:00 and 20:00 UTC for the closing imbalance and quarterly settlement. From 21:00 UTC the CME weekend halt removes any tradeable price path, so projected Tail falls to 8-10% across the final six slots and Stress settles into the low band. Every level beyond the current hour is conditional risk, not an assertion that future structure has already been observed.
